A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SR-NLE research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, algorithms, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original SR-NLE experiments across three datasets and four models, including unfaithfulness scores, ablations, and refinement analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds random-word feedback results, word-selection diagnostics, and detailed refinement case studies.

M1.justification: The prediction, explanation, feedback, refinement, attribution, and semantic-centroid procedures remain unchanged. Algorithms 1–3 and all six prompt templates match substantively; revised notation and expanded attribution explanations do not change the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ComVE, ECQA, and e-SNLI with the same task requirements and dataset coverage. The new diagnostics and random-feedback control reuse existing tasks and counterfactual inputs.

E2.justification: v2 adds random-word selection as an evaluated comparator against IWF-Pmt, IWF-Attn, and IWF-IG in Tables 12–13. Init-NLE, SC-NLE, and the separately reported G-TEX comparison remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix F.6 introduces a supplemental protocol using five randomly selected feedback words and three refinement rounds on e-SNLI across four models. New diagnostics measure selected-word hallucination, intervened-word inclusion, and full versus unique input lengths. Existing splits, models, decoding, interventions, and main experimental settings are retained.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands diagnostic analysis: random-word controls test dependence on selection quality, inclusion rates examine whether selectors recover the intervention, and hallucination rates assess input grounding. It also adds input-length analysis and complete NLF versus IWF-Attn case studies across all three datasets. Existing ablations are retained.

E5.justification: v2 newly reports averaging the random-word experiment over three seeds, with mean and standard deviation in Table 12. v1 contains no corresponding seed-based uncertainty reporting, and uncertainty is not added to the retained main results.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in the main and intermediate unfaithfulness tables are unchanged, but v2 adds substantial diagnostic results and qualitative refinement trajectories. For example, Table 12 reports e-SNLI averages of 29.28% for random feedback, 30.10% for IWF-Pmt, and 27.69% for IWF-Attn; Tables 9, 11, and 13 add length, hallucination, and intervention-inclusion results.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(10) and the algorithms retain the same mathematical content. Changes such as k/n becoming K/N are notational. The added empirical diagnostics introduce no substantive formal derivation, assumption, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: training-free self-refinement improves post-hoc explanation faithfulness, IWF outperforms NLF, and the best average unfaithfulness rate is 36.02% versus 54.81% initially. Additional evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: The mechanism interpretation changes substantially. v1 interprets comparable IWF scores as evidence of models' inherent ability to identify important reasoning components. v2 emphasizes robustness to different selectors; Appendix F.6 attributes much of the benefit to refinement despite imperfect or random word selection and identifies limitations in attribution quality. The existing limitations section is otherwise substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 newly states code availability and supplies a repository URL in the abstract. Existing model versions, attribution implementations, integration-step settings, and complete prompts are retained. The PDFs establish the added access information, not independently verified repository availability.

R1.justification: v2 expands attribution-related positioning, discussing AMPLIFY and Self-AMPLIFY and explicitly crediting the latter in the method description. It adds supporting citations concerning explanation generation and attribution evaluation. The principal contrasts with Cross-Refine and G-TEX remain intact.

P1.justification: The revision makes targeted prose edits, clarifies the evaluation description, standardizes terminology and notation, and expands the attribution rationale. Additional analysis subsections and a case-study appendix are inserted, while the main section sequence and most existing prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds four diagnostic tables and four case-study displays, including complete side-by-side refinement trajectories. It rearranges Figure 10 from a horizontal row into larger vertically stacked radar charts and adds best/second-best highlighting to the intermediate-results table. Existing diagrams and plots also receive localized caption, label, and placement changes.

improvement.justification: The random-word control and inclusion analysis directly examine the attribution mechanism, while worked examples, clearer research positioning, and code-access information improve transparency. These gains are limited by new reporting inconsistencies: Table 11's percentage label conflicts with the stated 3.75% average, and Appendix F.6 describes random feedback as worse although Table 12 places it ahead of IWF-Pmt. The added diagnostic evidence nevertheless provides a modest net improvement.
